relation_to_original_tuscan2_target: The primary target remains the original Tuscan-2 square of order 11. Every Tuscan-2(11) square is in particular eleven Hamilton rows with all 110 ordered linear adjacencies distinct, so it lies in the support ladder. Each ladder exclusion above (accepted, or written and unreviewed) is therefore a NECESSARY-CASE exclusion: a Tuscan-2(11) square, if one exists, would have to avoid it too. None of it is a construction, a sufficiency result or a nonexistence result. No distance-two event is used in v46-v59, and the literal Tuscan-1(11) control of v24 (support m=36) shows that distance-one reasoning alone cannot decide the target. The target needs either a literal 11x11 table with 110 distinct LINEAR distance-one and 99 distinct LINEAR distance-two events, or a contradiction for every arbitrary array that uses the distance-two condition. Neither is supplied. No normalized Latin/cyclic ansatz, global no-go or table is claimed or promoted.
